readings.title: Holiness in the Home
readings.subtitle: Family Statutes and Rights
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:10] When you go out to battle against your enemies, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given them into your hand, and you shall take them captive, [11] and shall see among the captives a woman fair of form, and shall delight in her and take her for your wife, [12] then you shall bring her home to your house, and she shall shave <dn>את</dn> her head and trim <dn>את</dn> her nails, [13] and put off <dn>את</dn> the clothes of her captivity, and shall dwell in your house, and mourn <dn>את</dn> her father and <dn>את</dn> her mother a month of days. And after that you shall go in to her and be her husband, and she shall be your wife. [14] And it shall be, if you are not pleased with her, then you shall let her go at her desire. But you do not sell her at all for silver, do not treat her harshly, because you have humbled her. [15] When a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and they have borne him children, both the loved and the unloved, and the first-born son is of her who is unloved, [16] then it shall be, on the day he makes <dn>את</dn> his sons inherit <dn>את</dn> what he has, he is not allowed to treat the son of the loved wife as the first-born in the face of the son of the unloved, who is truly the first-born. [17] But he is to acknowledge <dn>את</dn> the son of the unloved as the first-born by giving him a double portion of all that he has, for he is the beginning of his strength, the right of the first-born is his. [18] When a man has a wayward and rebellious son who does not listen to the voice of his father or the voice of his mother, and who, when they have disciplined him, does not listen to them, [19] then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city, to the gate of his city, [20] and shall say to the elders of his city, ‘This son of ours is wayward and rebellious, he does not listen to our voice, he is a glutton and a drunkard.’ [21] Then all the men of his city shall stone him with stones until he dies. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst, and let all Yisra’ĕl hear and fear.

readings.title: Community Integrity
readings.subtitle: Kindness, Order, and Distinctions
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:22] And when a man has committed a sin worthy of death, and he is put to death, and you shall hang <dn>את</dn> him on a tree, [23] his body shall not remain overnight on the tree, for you shall certainly bury him the same day – for he who is hanged is accursed of <dn>Elohim</dn> – so that you do not defile <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you for an inheritance. [Deuteronomy 22:1] You shall not see <dn>את</dn> your brother’s ox or <dn>את</dn> his sheep going astray, and ignore them – you shall certainly return them to your brother. [2] And if your brother is not near you, or if you do not know him, then you shall bring it to your own house, and it shall be with you until your brother seeks it, then you shall return it to him. [3] And so you do with his donkey, and so you do with his garment, and so you do with whatever your brother loses, which he has lost and you have found. You are not allowed to ignore it. [4] You shall not see <dn>את</dn> your brother’s donkey or his ox fall down on the way, and ignore them – you shall certainly help him to lift them up. [5] A woman does not wear that which pertains to a man, nor does a man put on a woman’s garment, for whoever does this is an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [6] When a bird’s nest happens to be before you on the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young ones or eggs, and the mother sitting on the young ones or on the eggs, do not take the mother with the young ones. [7] You shall certainly let <dn>את</dn> the mother go, and take <dn>את</dn> the young ones for yourself, so that it might be well with you and that you prolong your days. [8] When you build a new house, then you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring blood-guilt on your house if any one should fall from it. [9] Do not sow your vineyard with different kinds of seed, lest the yield of the seed which you have sown and the fruit of your vineyard be defiled. [10] Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together. [11] Do not wear a mixture of wool and linen together. [12] Make tassels on the four corners of the garment with which you cover yourself.

readings.title: The Sanctity of Marriage
readings.subtitle: Purity and Protection of the Bed
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 22:13] When a man takes a wife, and shall go in to her, and shall hate her, [14] and shall make up charges against her, and bring an evil name on her, and say, ‘I took this woman, and when I came near her I did not find her tokens of maidenhood,’ [15] then the father and mother of the young woman shall take and bring out <dn>את</dn> the tokens of the young woman’s maidenhood to the elders of the city at the gate. [16] And the young woman’s father shall say to the elders, ‘I gave <dn>את</dn> my daughter to this man as a wife, and he hates her. [17] ‘And see, he has made up charges, saying, “I did not find your daughter’s tokens of maidenhood,” and yet these are the tokens of my daughter’s maidenhood.’ And they shall spread the cloth before the elders of the city. [18] ‘Then the elders of that city shall take <dn>את</dn> that man and punish <dn>את</dn> him, [19] and fine him one hundred sheqels of silver and give them to the father of the young woman, because he has brought an evil name on a maiden of Yisra’ĕl. And she is to be his wife, he is not allowed to put her away all his days. [20] But if the matter is true, that the tokens of maidenhood were not found for the young woman, [21] then they shall bring out <dn>את</dn> the young woman to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones until she dies, because she has done wickedness in Yisra’ĕl, to play the whore in her father’s house. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [22] When a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, then both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman, and the woman. Thus you shall purge the evil from Yisra’ĕl. [23] When a young woman, a maiden, is engaged to a husband, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her, [24] then you shall bring <dn>את</dn> them both out to the gate of that city, and shall stone them with stones until they die, the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he has humbled <dn>את</dn> his neighbour’s wife. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [25] But if a man finds <dn>את</dn> an engaged young woman in the field, and the man seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die. [26] But you do nothing to the young woman, there is no sin in the young woman worthy of death, for as when a man rises against his neighbour and kills his being, so is this matter. [27] For he found her in the field, and the engaged young woman cried out, but there was no one to save her. [28] When a man finds a young woman, a maiden who is not engaged, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are found out, [29] then the man who lay with her shall give to the young woman’s father fifty sheqels of silver, and she is to be his wife because he has humbled her. He is not allowed to put her away all his days. [30] A man does not take <dn>את</dn> his father’s wife, nor uncover his father’s skirt.

readings.title: Sanctity in the Camp
readings.subtitle: Assembly Admission and Camp Purity
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:1] He who is emasculated by crushing or cutting shall not enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [2] One of illegitimate birth shall not enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even to the tenth generation he does not enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] An Ammonite or Mo’aḇite shall not enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, even to the tenth generation they do not enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> forever, [4] because they did not meet <dn>את</dn> you with bread and with water on the way when you came out of Mitsrayim, and because they hired against you <dn>את</dn> Bil’am son of Be’or from Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse you. [5] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> would not listen to Bil’am, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> turned <dn>את</dn> the curse into a blessing for you, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> loved you. [6] Do not seek their peace or their good all your days, forever. [7] Do not abominate an Eḏomite, for he is your brother. Do not abominate a Mitsrite, because you were a stranger in his land. [8] The children of the third generation born to them may enter the assembly of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [9] When the camp goes out against your enemies, then you shall guard yourself from every evil matter. [10] When there is any man among you who is not clean because of an emission by night, then he shall go outside the camp, he does not come into the midst of the camp. [11] And it shall be, when evening comes, that he washes with water. And when the sun goes down, he comes into the midst of the camp. [12] And you shall have a place outside the camp, where you shall go out. [13] And you shall have a sharp implement among your equipment, and it shall be, when you sit down outside, you shall dig with it and turn and cover <dn>את</dn> your excrement. [14] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and give your enemies over to you. Therefore your camp shall be set-apart, so that <dn>He</dn> does not see an unclean matter among you, and shall turn away from you.

readings.title: Social Right-Rulings
readings.subtitle: Statutes of Conduct and Compassion
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 23:15] Do not hand over to his master the slave who has escaped from his master to you. [16] Let him dwell with you, in your midst, in the place which he chooses within one of your gates, where it is good for him. Do not oppress him. [17] There shall be no ritual whore among the daughters of Yisra’ĕl, nor a ritual whore among the sons of Yisra’ĕl. [18] Do not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> for any vowing, for both of these are an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [19] Do not lend on interest to your brother – interest of silver or interest of food or interest of whatever is lent on interest. [20] To a foreigner you may lend on interest, but to your brother you do not lend on interest, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> blesses you in all that you set your hand to in the land which you are entering to possess. [21] When you make a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, do not delay to pay it, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall certainly require it of you, and it shall be sin in you. [22] But if you abstain from vowing, it is not sin in you. [23] That which has gone out of your lips you shall guard and do, for you voluntarily vowed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> what you have promised with your mouth. [24] When you come into your neighbour’s vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes at your desire, but do not put any in your vessel. [25] When you come into your neighbour’s standing grain, you may pluck the heads with your hand, but do not use a sickle on your neighbour’s standing grain. [Deuteronomy 24:1] When a man takes a wife and shall marry her, then it shall be, if she finds no favour in his eyes because he has found a matter of nakedness in her, and he shall write her a bill of divorce, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house, [2] and she shall leave his house and go and become another man’s wife, [3] and the latter husband shall hate her and write her a bill of divorce, and put it in her hand, and send her out of his house, or if the latter husband dies who took her as his wife, [4] then her former husband who sent her away is not allowed to take her back to be his wife after she has been defiled, for that is an abomination before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And do not bring sin on <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance.

readings.title: Justice for the Vulnerable
readings.subtitle: Pledges, Wages, and Fairness
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 24:5] When a man has taken a new wife, he does not go out to battle nor is any matter imposed on him. He shall be free at home one year, and shall rejoice with <dn>את</dn> his wife whom he has taken. [6] No one shall take in pledge a lower or an upper millstone, for he takes a life in pledge. [7] When a man is found kidnapping any of his brothers of the children of Yisra’ĕl, and treats him harshly or sells him, then that kidnapper shall die. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [8] Take heed, in an outbreak of leprosy, to diligently guard and do according to all that the priests, the Lĕwites, teach you. As I have commanded them, so you shall guard to do. [9] Remember <dn>את</dn> what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> did to Miryam on the way when you were coming out of Mitsrayim. [10] When you lend your brother any loan, do not go into his house to get his pledge. [11] Stand outside, and let the man to whom you lend bring <dn>את</dn> the pledge out to you. [12] And if the man is poor, do not sleep with his pledge. [13] You shall certainly return <dn>את</dn> the pledge to him when the sun goes down, and he shall sleep in his own garment, and shall bless you. And it shall be righteousness to you before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [14] Do not oppress a hired servant who is poor and needy, of your brothers or of the strangers who are in your land within your gates. [15] Give him his wages on the same day, and do not let the sun go down on it, for he is poor and lifts up his being to it, so that he does not cry out against you to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and it shall be sin in you. [16] Fathers are not put to death for their children, and children are not put to death for their fathers, each shall be put to death for his own sin. [17] Do not distort the right-ruling of a stranger or the fatherless, nor take a widow’s garment in pledge. [18] And you shall remember that you were a slave in Mitsrayim, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> redeemed you from there. Therefore I am commanding you to do <dn>את</dn> this matter. [19] When you reap <dn>את</dn> your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, do not go back to get it. Let it be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow, so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</DL blesses you in all the work of your hands. [20] When you beat your olive trees, do not go over the branches again. Let it be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow. [21] When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not glean it afterward. Let it be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow. [22] And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Mitsrayim. Therefore I am commanding you to do <dn>את</dn> this matter.

readings.title: Righteous Measure
readings.subtitle: Corporal Punishment, Levirate Duty, and Amalĕq
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 25:1] When there is a dispute between men, and they come into court, and the judges judge them, and shall declare <dn>את</dn> the righteous to be right and <dn>את</dn> the wrong to be wrong, [2] then it shall be, if the wrong one is worthy of a beating, that the judge shall cause him to lie down and be beaten in his presence with the number of blows according to his wrong. [3] He gives him forty blows, he does not add, lest he should add many more blows than these, and your brother be humbled before your eyes. [4] Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing. [5] When brothers dwell together, and one of them has died and has no son, the widow of the dead man shall not become the wife of a stranger outside. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, and shall take her as his wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her. [6] And it shall be that the first-born son which she bears shall stand in the name of his dead brother, so that his name is not blotted out of Yisra’ĕl. [7] But if the man does not desire to take his brother’s wife, then his brother’s wife shall go up to the gate to the elders, and say, ‘My husband’s brother refuses to raise up a name to his brother in Yisra’ĕl, he does not desire to perform the duty of my husband’s brother.’ [8] Then the elders of his city shall call him and speak to him. And if he stands and says, ‘I do not desire to take her,’ [9] then his brother’s wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, and shall remove his sandal from his foot, and shall spit in his face, and shall answer and say, ‘Thus it is done to the man who does not build up his brother’s house.’ [10] And his name shall be called in Yisra’ĕl, ‘The house of him whose sandal was removed.’ [11] When men fight with one another, a man and his brother, and the wife of one shall draw near to deliver <dn>את</dn> her husband from the hand of the one smiting him, and shall put out <dn>את</dn> her hand and take him by his genitals, [12] then you shall cut off her hand, your eye does not pardon. [13] You shall not have in your bag different weights, a great and a small. [14] You shall not have in your house different measures, a great and a small. [15] Have a perfect and right weight, have a perfect and right measure, so that your days are prolonged in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you. [16] For all who do these, all who do unrighteously, are an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [17] Remember <dn>את</dn> what Amalĕq did to you on the way as you were coming out of Mitsrayim, [18] how he met you on the way and smote the stragglers, all the feeble ones in your rear, when you were tired and weary, and he did not fear <dn>Elohim</dn>. [19] And it shall be, when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you rest from all your enemies all around, in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess as an inheritance, that you shall blot out <dn>את</dn> the remembrance of Amalĕq from under the heavens. Do not forget!
